subject: chem
title: Nitrogen and Sulfur Chemistry
subtitle: Nitrogen cycle, industrial chemistry, sulfur compounds and acid rain.
concept: The Haber process makes ammonia from N₂ and H₂; conditions are a compromise between yield (lower T) and rate (higher T).
Nitric acid is made by the Ostwald process (catalytic oxidation of NH₃).
Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides cause acid rain; their effects and control are important environmental topics.

notes.heading: Haber Process
items: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)   ΔH = −92 kJ mol⁻¹. The reaction is exothermic and produces fewer moles of gas.

Industrial conditions — a compromise: 450 °C (lower T increases Kc and yield, but the rate is too slow without the Fe catalyst; 450 °C gives an acceptable rate with ≈15% yield); 200 atm (shifts equilibrium toward NH₃; lower pressure would reduce yield; higher pressure is technically demanding and costly); Fe catalyst (speeds up equilibration without changing Kc); NH₃ is liquefied and removed continuously (shifts equilibrium right — Le Chatelier).

notes.heading: Ostwald Process and Nitric Acid
items: Step 1: catalytic oxidation of ammonia — 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O (Pt/Rh catalyst, ~900 °C). Step 2: further oxidation — 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂. Step 3: absorption in water — 3NO₂ + H₂O → 2HNO₃ + NO (NO recycled back to Step 2).

notes.heading: Acid Rain and Sulfur Chemistry
items: SO₂ from burning fossil fuels (sulfur impurities) dissolves in rainwater to form sulfurous acid, which is further oxidised to sulfuric acid. NOₓ from vehicle engines (N₂ + O₂ at high T) forms nitric acid. Both lower the pH of precipitation below 5.6 (normal rain, already slightly acidic from CO₂).
Effects of acid rain: acidification of lakes and soil; damage to limestone and marble buildings (CaCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + CO₂ + H₂O); forest damage.

Controls: flue gas desulfurisation (scrubbing flue gases with CaO/Ca(OH)₂ — CaO + SO₂ → CaSO₃); catalytic converters in vehicles (Pt/Rh/Pd — oxidise CO and unburned hydrocarbons, reduce NOₓ to N₂ and O₂); low-sulfur fuels.

definitions.body: Industrial synthesis of ammonia: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) using Fe catalyst at 450°C and 200 atm.
Precipitation with pH below 5.6 due to dissolved SO₂ and NOₓ from burning fossil fuels and vehicle emissions.
Device fitted to vehicle exhausts containing Pt, Rh or Pd catalysts that convert CO, hydrocarbons and NOₓ to CO₂, H₂O and N₂.

workedExamples.q: Explain why the Haber process uses 450°C rather than a lower temperature.

steps.text: The reaction is exothermic; Le Chatelier → lower T increases Kc (higher equilibrium yield of NH₃).
However, at lower temperatures, the rate of reaction is too slow to be economically viable, even with the Fe catalyst.
450°C is a compromise: Kc is lower (yield ~15%) but the reaction rate is fast enough for continuous industrial production. NH₃ is continuously removed to shift equilibrium right.

mistakes: Saying a catalyst increases yield in the Haber process — it does not; it only speeds up reaching equilibrium.
Confusing the conditions for the Haber process (450°C, 200 atm, Fe) with the Contact process (450°C, 1–2 atm, V₂O₅).
Stating acid rain has pH below 7 — it must be below 5.6 (normal rain is already slightly acidic at ~5.6 due to CO₂).
tips: Haber conditions mnemonic: '450, 200, Fe' — temperature, pressure, catalyst.
For acid rain questions: name the gas (SO₂ or NOₓ), its source, the acid formed, and one effect/control.
Contact process uses low pressure (1–2 atm) because the yield is already high at this pressure; higher P would be costly for little gain.

flashcards.q: State the conditions for the Haber process.
flashcards.a: 450°C; 200 atm; iron (Fe) catalyst; ammonia continuously removed.

flashcards.q: Why is 200 atm used in the Haber process?
flashcards.a: Fewer moles of gas on the right (2 vs 4) — high pressure shifts equilibrium toward NH₃ (Le Chatelier); increases yield and rate.
SO₂ (from burning sulfur-containing fuels) and NOₓ (from vehicle engines/lightning) dissolve in rainwater forming H₂SO₄ and HNO₃.

flashcards.q: How do catalytic converters reduce pollution?
flashcards.a: Pt/Rh/Pd catalysts convert: 2CO + 2NO → 2CO₂ + N₂; unburned hydrocarbons are oxidised to CO₂ + H₂O.

flashcards.q: What is the role of V₂O₅ in the Contact process?
flashcards.a: Catalyst for the oxidation of SO₂ to SO₃: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃.

flashcards.q: Why isn't SO₃ absorbed directly into water in the Contact process?
flashcards.a: SO₃ + H₂O produces a corrosive acid mist that is hard to handle — SO₃ is first absorbed into concentrated H₂SO₄ to form oleum.

questions.q: Why is a catalyst used in the Haber process?
questions.exp: A catalyst lowers activation energy and speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally — equilibrium is reached faster but Kc (and yield) are unchanged.

questions.q: What is the catalyst in the Haber process?
questions.exp: The Haber process uses iron (Fe) as the heterogeneous catalyst.

questions.q: Which gas from vehicle engines contributes to acid rain?
questions.exp: Nitric oxide (NO) forms at high temperatures in engines (N₂ + O₂ → 2NO); it is oxidised to NO₂ then dissolves in rainwater to form HNO₃.

questions.q: What happens in flue gas desulfurisation?
opts: CaO reacts with SO₂ to form CaSO₃
NO is removed by activated charcoal
CO₂ is captured in liquid ammonia
questions.exp: Calcium oxide (or hydroxide) reacts with SO₂: CaO + SO₂ → CaSO₃, removing SO₂ from power station emissions.

questions.q: In the Contact process, why is low pressure (1–2 atm) used rather than high pressure?
opts: High pressure is not needed — yield is already high; high P is costly
V₂O₅ only works at low pressure
SO₃ is unstable at high pressure
questions.exp: The equilibrium yield is already high at low pressure; high pressure equipment is expensive and the marginal gain in yield doesn't justify the cost.

questions.q: What are the operating conditions of the Haber process?
questions.exp: 450 °C (compromise between yield and rate), 200 atm (shifts equilibrium toward fewer moles of gas), Fe catalyst (speeds up equilibration). Lower T increases Kc but rate is too slow; the 450 °C/Fe combination gives a usable rate with ~15% conversion.

questions.q: In the Ostwald process, what catalyst is used to oxidise ammonia?
questions.exp: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O. A Pt/Rh gauze catalyst at ~900 °C is used. Platinum-rhodium alloy withstands the high temperature and provides excellent surface area for catalysis.

questions.q: What is the main source of SO₂ causing acid rain?
opts: Burning fossil fuels containing sulfur impurities
questions.exp: Fossil fuels (especially coal and oil) contain sulfur as an impurity. When burned, S + O₂ → SO₂. SO₂ dissolves in rainwater to form sulfurous acid (H₂SO₃), further oxidised to sulfuric acid — causing acid rain.

questions.q: How does flue gas desulfurisation (FGD) reduce SO₂ emissions?
opts: By burning fuel at lower temperatures
By scrubbing flue gases with calcium oxide or slaked lime, forming calcium sulfite/sulfate
By adding nitrogen to the combustion gases
questions.exp: CaO + SO₂ → CaSO₃ (or Ca(OH)₂ + SO₂ → CaSO₃ + H₂O). The calcium sulfite can be further oxidised to CaSO₄ (gypsum). FGD removes >95% of SO₂ from power station emissions.

questions.q: In the Contact process for H₂SO₄, what catalyst is used?
questions.exp: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ is catalysed by V₂O₅ at 450 °C and 1–2 atm. The SO₃ is then absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ (not water directly — the reaction is too violent) to form oleum, which is diluted to give H₂SO₄.

questions.q: Why is nitrogen in the atmosphere relatively unreactive?
opts: N₂ has a low bond enthalpy
N₂ has a very high bond enthalpy (945 kJ mol⁻¹) due to the triple bond
N₂ has no electrons available for bonding
questions.exp: The N≡N triple bond has a bond enthalpy of 945 kJ mol⁻¹ — one of the strongest bonds known. A large activation energy is needed to break it, making N₂ kinetically inert under normal conditions despite being thermodynamically feasible to react.

questions.q: The Haber process involves a reversible reaction. Why is ammonia removed continuously?
opts: To speed up the forward reaction rate directly
To shift the equilibrium to the right (Le Chatelier), increasing yield
To reduce pressure in the system
To prevent the catalyst from being poisoned
questions.exp: By continuously removing NH₃ (liquefied and collected), its concentration is kept low. By Le Chatelier's principle, the equilibrium shifts to the right to replace the removed product, increasing overall yield.

questions.q: Which gas is produced at both electrodes when dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed?
opts: H₂ at cathode, O₂ at anode
SO₂ at anode, H₂ at cathode
questions.exp: Cathode: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂ (H⁺ ions from H₂SO₄ and water). Anode: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ (water is oxidised; SO₄²⁻ is not discharged in dilute solution). The ratio is 2:1 H₂:O₂ by volume.

questions.q: What environmental effect does acid rain have on limestone buildings?
opts: CaCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + CO₂ + H₂O — the stone dissolves
It blackens but does not damage
questions.exp: CaCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + CO₂ + H₂O. The insoluble limestone reacts with sulfuric acid from acid rain. The calcium sulfate product is more soluble than limestone and is washed away, eroding the building's surface.

questions.q: Which best describes the role of NOₓ from vehicles in acid rain formation?
opts: NOₓ reacts directly with water in the atmosphere to form sulfuric acid
NOₓ is oxidised to NO₂ and dissolves with water to form nitric acid (HNO₃)
NOₓ only causes smog, not acid rain
NOₓ neutralises SO₂ in the atmosphere
questions.exp: Vehicle engines produce NO from N₂ + O₂ at high temperature. In the atmosphere: 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂; 3NO₂ + H₂O → 2HNO₃ + NO. The nitric acid contributes to acid rain alongside H₂SO₄.

questions.q: In the Haber process, what temperature is used as a compromise?
questions.exp: 450°C is a compromise: lower T favours equilibrium yield but is too slow; 450°C with Fe catalyst gives an acceptable rate (~15% yield).

questions.q: The Haber process uses iron as a catalyst. What does this change?
questions.exp: A catalyst increases the rate of both forward and reverse reactions equally — equilibrium is reached faster but the position (yield) is unchanged.

questions.q: What is the role of the V₂O₅ catalyst in the Contact process?
questions.exp: V₂O₅ catalyses the oxidation 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (step 2 of the Contact process), increasing the rate of reaching equilibrium.

questions.q: Why is SO₃ absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ rather than water in the Contact process?
opts: Direct absorption in water produces dangerous acid mist
questions.exp: SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄ is very exothermic. Direct addition to water produces a dangerous corrosive mist. Absorption in conc. H₂SO₄ gives oleum, which is then diluted safely.

questions.q: Acid rain is primarily caused by which gases?
questions.exp: SO₂ (from burning fossil fuels) and NOₓ (from vehicle engines and combustion) dissolve in rainwater forming sulfuric and nitric acids, lowering pH below 5.6.

questions.q: Flue gas desulfurisation removes SO₂ using:
questions.exp: CaO/Ca(OH)₂ is reacted with SO₂: CaO + SO₂ → CaSO₃. This removes SO₂ before it reaches the atmosphere.

questions.q: In the Ostwald process, ammonia is first oxidised over a Pt/Rh catalyst to give:
questions.exp: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O (over Pt/Rh at ~900°C). NO is then further oxidised to NO₂ and absorbed in water to give HNO₃.

questions.q: Which process uses nitrogen and hydrogen to manufacture ammonia?
questions.exp: The Haber process: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. Conditions: 450°C, 200 atm, iron catalyst. Used to make fertilisers.

questions.q: Increasing pressure in the Haber process increases yield because:
opts: There are fewer moles of gas on the product side
questions.exp: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: 4 mol gas → 2 mol gas. Higher pressure shifts equilibrium toward fewer moles (Le Chatelier) — toward NH₃.

questions.q: Catalytic converters in vehicles reduce which harmful emission?
questions.exp: Pt/Rh/Pd catalysts convert NOₓ → N₂ + O₂ and CO → CO₂, and oxidise unburned hydrocarbons. All three classes of pollutant are reduced.

recall: State the conditions and equation for the Haber process.
Explain the industrial compromise temperature of 450°C.
Describe the Ostwald process for manufacturing nitric acid.
Explain the causes and effects of acid rain.
Describe two methods used to reduce acid rain.

summary.label: Catalyst
summary.value: speeds rate; doesn't change Kc or yield
